preserved_constraints.text: 肝脏肿瘤分割目前有哪些技术瓶颈？

claims.text: 现有证据仅有一篇摘要直接涉及肝脏肿瘤CT分割，且只笼统列举了挑战，未系统比较或量化各项技术瓶颈；因此只能给出该摘要所述层面的瓶颈，无法据此形成完整的瓶颈清单或优先级排序。
limitations: 仅摘要级证据，未提供全文方法细节或消融分析

claims.text: 该摘要指出，CT图像中肝脏肿瘤的分割与分类面临噪声、边界不清、组织异质性，以及肿瘤组织外观、形状、大小和位置变异大等困难。
limitations: 挑战为作者概括性陈述，未逐项量化其对分割性能的影响

claims.text: 针对上述困难，该研究采用改进的Dense U-Net进行肿瘤分割，并用基于预训练VGG-16的深度CNN区分正常与恶性肝脏肿瘤。
limitations: 摘要未说明网络结构细节、训练策略或预处理方式

claims.text: 在MICCAI 2017 LiTS挑战数据集上，该研究报告分割Dice为95.40%、Jaccard指数为92%、准确率为92.60%；分类模型准确率96%、敏感度95.80%、特异度96.20%、精确率95.80%。
limitations: 仅为单一数据集上的摘要报告结果，未提供外部验证或与其他方法的对照

claims.text: 所提供证据未涉及跨中心/跨设备泛化、小肿瘤与边界病灶的分割误差、标注依赖、类别不平衡或临床部署等瓶颈，这些方面在本证据集中均未见报道，不能据此判断其是否构成实际瓶颈。
limitations: 缺失为检索证据范围内的缺失，不代表原文献全文未讨论

claims.text: 基于该摘要，可推测未来工作需针对边界不清与形态变异大的肿瘤改进分割鲁棒性，并在多来源数据上验证；这属于推断，而非文献已报告的研究结论。

openalex_record.title: Automatic segmentation and classification of the liver tumor using deep learning algorithms
openalex_record.journal: International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication, Embedded and Secure Systems (ACCESS)
openalex_record.abstract: Liver tumors are one of the life-threatening cancers with the fastest-growth rates worldwide. Early detection of tumors may therefore reduce morbidity and increase the survival rate. The development of automated techniques for the precise segmentation of hepatic tumors is essential for assisting doctors in tumor diagnosis and preoperative planning for surgical treatment of the liver which reduces the risk of surgical resection. The classification and segmentation of hepatic tumors in Computerized Tomography (CT) scan pose a great challenge due to noise, unclear boundaries, heterogeneity, and variability in tumor tissue appearance, shape, size, and location. In this study, we describe a novel method for automatic segmentation and classification of hepatic tumors in CT scan images using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks. For tumor segmentation, we created a modified Dense U-net model. The classification framework is based on a novel deep CNN with a pre-trained VGG-16 network to distinguish between normal and malignant liver tumors. The proposed system was evaluated based on MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) Challenge dataset and obtained the best result with a Dice Score of 95.40%, Jaccard Index of 92%, and accuracy of 92.60% for segmentation and the classification model has achieved an accuracy of 96%, Sensitivity of 95.80%, Specificity of 96.20% and Precision of 95.80%.

sources.title: Automatic segmentation and classification of the liver tumor using deep learning algorithms
sources.journal: International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication, Embedded and Secure Systems (ACCESS)

evidence.text: Liver tumors are one of the life-threatening cancers with the fastest-growth rates worldwide. Early detection of tumors may therefore reduce morbidity and increase the survival rate. The development of automated techniques for the precise segmentation of hepatic tumors is essential for assisting doctors in tumor diagnosis and preoperative planning for surgical treatment of the liver which reduces the risk of surgical resection. The classification and segmentation of hepatic tumors in Computerized Tomography (CT) scan pose a great challenge due to noise, unclear boundaries, heterogeneity, and variability in tumor tissue appearance, shape, size, and location. In this study, we describe a novel method for automatic segmentation and classification of hepatic tumors in CT scan images using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks. For tumor segmentation, we created a modified Dense U-net model. The classification framework is based on a novel deep CNN with a pre-trained VGG-16 network to distinguish between normal and malignant liver tumors. The proposed system was evaluated based on MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) Challenge dataset and obtained the best result with a Dice Score of 95.40%, Jaccard Index of 92%, and accuracy of 92.60% for segmentation and the classification model has achieved an accuracy of 96%, Sensitivity of 95.80%, Specificity of 96.20% and Precision of 95.80%.

assessments.quote: we introduce a generative model representing the formation of liver CT images and employ it for segmentation of hepatic tumors
assessments.reason: Liver tumor segmentation task matches population and task, but abstract describes a generative model and comparison, not bottlenecks, limitations, open problems or future directions. Useful as a segmentation method paper but indirect for the bottleneck question.

assessments.quote: The classification and segmentation of hepatic tumors in Computerized Tomography (CT) scan pose a great challenge due to noise, unclear boundaries, heterogeneity, and variability in tumor tissue appearance, shape, size, and location.
assessments.reason: Explicitly names technical challenges for hepatic tumor segmentation in CT (noise, unclear boundaries, heterogeneity, variability), matching population and task. It also proposes a segmentation method, but the challenge statement directly supports the bottleneck question.

assessments.quote: Automatic hepatic tumor segmentation is a crucial step for diagnosis and surgery planning.
assessments.reason: Liver tumor segmentation task matches, but the abstract presents a knowledge-based automatic method and results without discussing bottlenecks, limitations, open problems or future directions.

assessments.quote: the authors compare the accuracy of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) implementations of a computer-aided image segmentation method
assessments.reason: Hepatic tumor segmentation and volumetrics match population and task, but the abstract is a 2D vs 3D method comparison and does not address technical bottlenecks, limitations, open problems or future directions.

assessments.quote: Este artículo de revisión presenta un análisis del estado del arte en procesamiento de imágenes médicas mediante conjuntos neutrosóficos

assessments.quote: noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
assessments.reason: Downstream classification/differentiation of HCC vs MF-ICC, not liver tumor segmentation. Task mismatch.

assessments.quote: Without having a reference image and training data, fully automatic segmentation of the liver structure and tumors using a reference point based on the spine is processed.
assessments.reason: Proposes point-based liver and hepatic tumor segmentation in CE-CT, matching population and task. However, the abstract describes a method and evaluation metrics without discussing technical bottlenecks, limitations, open problems, or future directions, so it is only indirectly useful for the bottleneck question.

assessments.quote: This system has concentrated on finding a fast and interactive segmentation method for liver and tumor segmentation.
assessments.reason: Presents a graph-cut based liver and hepatic tumor segmentation method, matching population and task. The abstract does not discuss technical challenges, limitations, open problems, or future directions, so it is only partial evidence for the bottleneck question.

assessments.quote: Preoperative vessel segmentation in the patient's liver region has become an increasingly important and challenging problem.
assessments.reason: The segmentation target is hepatic veins and arterial vessels in liver tumor patients, not liver tumors themselves. It mentions vessel segmentation challenges and proposes extension to liver tumor segmentation, but the task/population alignment is indirect and no tumor segmentation bottleneck is evidenced.

assessments.quote: Comparative results with the state-of-the-art techniques on the same data show the competing performance of the proposed framework for simultaneous liver and tumor segmentation.
assessments.reason: Deep learning framework for simultaneous liver and hepatic tumor segmentation on LiTS, matching population and task. records.title: A Controlled Generative Model for Segmentation of Liver Tumors
records.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generative model representing the formation of liver CT images and employ it for segmentation of hepatic tumors. We extend the graphical model used in label fusion techniques for the segmentation of multi-modality Magnetic Resonance brain images. To resemble atlas data, we segment the first slice by a physician and propagate it for processing of subsequent slices. We include a knowledge-based constraint in the model that is considered as a key difference with classical generative models. We compared our method with conventional Bayesian techniques and state-of-the-art hepatic tumor segmentation algorithms. We achieved a measure of 0.86 ± 0.06 and 0.76 ± 0.09 regarding Dice and Jaccard metrics respectively that is better than recent researches.

records.title: Automatic segmentation and classification of the liver tumor using deep learning algorithms
records.journal: International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication, Embedded and Secure Systems (ACCESS)
records.abstract: Liver tumors are one of the life-threatening cancers with the fastest-growth rates worldwide. Early detection of tumors may therefore reduce morbidity and increase the survival rate. The development of automated techniques for the precise segmentation of hepatic tumors is essential for assisting doctors in tumor diagnosis and preoperative planning for surgical treatment of the liver which reduces the risk of surgical resection. The classification and segmentation of hepatic tumors in Computerized Tomography (CT) scan pose a great challenge due to noise, unclear boundaries, heterogeneity, and variability in tumor tissue appearance, shape, size, and location. In this study, we describe a novel method for automatic segmentation and classification of hepatic tumors in CT scan images using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks. For tumor segmentation, we created a modified Dense U-net model. The classification framework is based on a novel deep CNN with a pre-trained VGG-16 network to distinguish between normal and malignant liver tumors. The proposed system was evaluated based on MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) Challenge dataset and obtained the best result with a Dice Score of 95.40%, Jaccard Index of 92%, and accuracy of 92.60% for segmentation and the classification model has achieved an accuracy of 96%, Sensitivity of 95.80%, Specificity of 96.20% and Precision of 95.80%.

records.title: Automatic liver tumor segmentation from CT scans with knowledge-based constraints
records.abstract: Automatic hepatic tumor segmentation is a crucial step for diagnosis and surgery planning. This paper presents a new fully automatic technique to segment the tumors in liver structure with no interaction from user. Contrast enhancement is applied to the slices of segmented liver, then adding each image to itself to have a white image with some pepper noise and tumors as dark gray spots. After applying Gaussian smoothing, Isodata is used to threshold the tumor in the slice. In order to eliminate erroneous segmentation, discriminative rule based on diagnostic knowledge on liver cancer shape is applied along with a 3-D consistency check is performed based on three-dimensional information that a lesion mass cannot appear in a single slice independently. Tests are performed on 9 abdominal datasets and promising result shows that sensitivity and specificity for automatic liver tumor segmentation are 87% and 99% respectively.

records.title: Comparison of two‐dimensional and three‐dimensional iterative watershed segmentation methods in hepatic tumor volumetrics
records.abstract: In this work the authors compare the accuracy of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) implementations of a computer-aided image segmentation method to that of physician observers (using manual outlining) for volume measurements of liver tumors visualized with diagnostic contrast-enhanced and PET/CT-based non-contrast-enhanced (PET-CT) CT scans. The method assessed is a hybridization of the watershed method using observer-set markers with a gradient vector flow approach. This method is known as the iterative watershed segmentation (IWS) method. Initial assessments are performed using software phantoms that model a range of tumor shapes, noise levels, and noise qualities. IWS is then applied to CT image sets of patients with identified hepatic tumors and compared to the physicians' manual outlines on the same tumors. The repeatability of the physicians' measurements is also assessed. IWS utilizes multiple levels of segmentation performed with the use of "fuzzy regions" that could be considered part of a selected tumor. In phantom studies, the outermost volume outline for level 1 (called level 1_1 consisting of inner region plus fuzzy region) was generally the most accurate. For in vivo studies, the level 1_1 and the second outermost outline for level 2 (called level 2_2 consisting of inner region plus two fuzzy regions) typically had the smallest percent error values when compared to physician observer volume estimates. Our data indicate that allowing the operator to choose the "best result" level iteration outline from all generated outlines would likely give the more accurate volume for a given tumor rather than automatically choosing a particular level iteration outline. The preliminary in vivo results indicate that 2D-IWS is likely to be more accurate than 3D-IWS in relation to the observer volume estimates.

records.title: Procesamiento de imágenes médicas mediante conjuntos neutrosóficos
records.abstract: El procesamiento de imágenes médicas constituye un área crítica para el diagnóstico, donde la incertidumbre y la ambigüedad inherentes a los datos biomédicos limitan la efectividad de los métodos convencionales. En este contexto, la teoría neutrosófica ha emergido como un marco matemático robusto para el manejo explícito de información imprecisa. Este artículo de revisión presenta un análisis del estado del arte en procesamiento de imágenes médicas mediante conjuntos neutrosóficos, abarcando sus fundamentos teóricos, las principales técnicas de preprocesamiento, segmentación y extracción de características, y su integración con modelos de inteligencia artificial y aprendizaje profundo. Asimismo, se examinan comparativamente sus ventajas frente a los métodos clásicos basados en lógica difusa, así como sus limitaciones actuales relacionadas con la escalabilidad, la automatización y la integración en flujos clínicos digitales. Finalmente, se discuten los retos y oportunidades futuras, destacando el potencial de la neutrosofía híbrida y explicable como herramienta clave para el desarrollo de sistemas médicos más precisos, interpretables y confiables en la medicina de precisión contemporánea.

records.title: Advances in Deep Learning and Image Processing for Brain Tumor Detection and Classification: A Comprehensive Review
records.journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology
records.abstract: Brain tumor identification and classification by the application of deep learning and sophisticated image-processing techniques have been receiving a lot of attention in the medical field. Accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient outcome rely on the accurate identification and differentiation of brain tumors, such as gliomas, meningiomas, and metastases. The most recent developments in deep learning-based techniques for brain tumor identification and categorization by applying medical imaging data, including Computed Tomography (CT). This study looks at CT and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). The main topic of this study is the general theory and developments in deep learning methods for the identification and classification of brain tumors. It investigates how the precision and efficacy of tumor detection can be increased through a variety of models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The paper emphasizes the Significance of applying novel deep-learning techniques for facilitating precise and automated brain tumor identification for individualized treatment, with an emphasis on important achievements, challenges, and opportunities in the area.

records.title: Robots for CT-guided needle insertion: clinical implementation and future perspectives
records.abstract: Robotic systems for computed tomography (CT)-guided needle insertion have been developed to address the limitations of conventional manual needle insertion. Thus far, various robotic systems have been clinically implemented, and accumulating evidence has suggested their clinical utility. The evidence has evolved beyond initial feasibility and early clinical experience to include larger observational and comparative studies. These studies have demonstrated high success rates of robot-assisted needle insertion in various CT-guided interventions, including thermal ablation, biopsy, and preoperative localization. Furthermore, an increasing number of comparative studies have demonstrated the advantages of robot-assisted procedures over conventional manual procedures. These advantages include improved needle insertion accuracy and reduced radiation doses to patients and/or physicians. Although most currently available robotic systems are needle-guiding robots designed to align a needle guide with a predetermined insertion trajectory, we have developed a CT-guided needle insertion robot capable of robotic needle advancement via remote control. Clinical studies have demonstrated the feasibility of robotic needle insertion using this system, as well as needle placement accuracy comparable to that of manual procedures, while eliminating radiation exposure to physicians. The integration of artificial intelligence and the implementation of telerobotic interventions are expected to contribute significantly to the further advancement of robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion. This narrative review summarizes the current clinical implementations and available evidence for robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion, including our system, and discusses future perspectives in this field.

records.title: Comprehensive motion management for liver SBRT on a 1.5 T MR-Linac: Initial clinical experience and dosimetric comparison with an ITV-based workflow
records.abstract: Background and purpose Respiratory-gated MR-guided workflows enable expiration-gated liver stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) based on real-time intrafraction target monitoring. We evaluated the dosimetric impact and early clinical feasibility of this approach by comparing clinically delivered expiration-gated plans with retrospectively generated non-gated ITV-based plans. Methods The first 20 consecutive patients treated with online adaptive MR-guided SBRT for primary or secondary liver malignancies on a 1.5 T MR-Linac between October 2024 and April 2025 were included. Five patients had two lesions, treated with separate plans in two patients, resulting in 22 matched plan pairs. For each clinically delivered gated plan, a retrospective ITV-based plan with identical prescription dose was generated. Paired differences were tested with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and p -values were adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. The dose–volume analysis was considered exploratory. Results Median planning target volume was lower with the gated workflow than with ITV-based planning (28.0 vs. 41.9 cc). Organ-at-risk constraint violations were fewer with the gated workflow (10 vs. 19), with 11 violations resolved and 2 newly occurring. PTV D98% did not differ significantly ( p = 0.41), although one gated and four ITV-based plans showed PTV D98% < 95%. Uninvolved liver dose was significantly lower with the gated workflow (median Dmean difference 0.97 Gy and 0.93 Gy for three- and five-fraction plans; adjusted p ≤ 0.037). Among 93 evaluable fractions, the mean plan-level median active delivery time was 7.6 min for three-fraction and 6.7 min for five-fraction treatments. Conclusion Expiration-gated MR-guided liver SBRT reduced target volumes and improved normal tissue sparing without compromising target coverage or routine clinical feasibility.

records.title: Reviewer #2 (Public review): An Itch Receptor Drives Melanoma
records.abstract: Mas-Related GPCR X4 (MRGPRX4) is a sensory neuron-restricted receptor for cholestatic itch. Here, we identify MRGPRX4 as an unexpected melanoma driver. MRGPRX4 is upregulated in melanoma and is confined to invasive, neural-crest-like and pre-EMT states associated with dedifferentiation and therapy resistance. Ectopic MRGPRX4 expression in mouse melanocytes drives 100% penetrant, highly metastatic melanoma, demonstrating oncogenic behavior. MRGPRX4 promotes melanoma cell proliferation and invasion through basal, ligand-independent, PI3K-AKT-MAPK activation. Multi-omics links MRGPRX4 expression to a mesenchymal/neural-crest–like program that defines a distinct invasive MRGPRX4+ niche. Comparing transcptomics of MRGPRX4-driven tumors shows a broad overlap with BRAF/NRAS-driven tumors; however, the MRGPRX4 model also enriches an ECM-rich, invasive neural crest–like melanoma state. MRGPRX4 further remodels the tumor microenvironment toward an immunosuppressive, checkpoint-high state enriched in suppressive myeloid cells. Pharmacologic MRGPRX4 inhibition suppresses basal signaling and limits melanoma growth and invasion. In sum, melanoma exploits MRGPRX4 to acquire an invasive and immunosuppressive phenotype, nominating this somatosensory GPCR as a promising therapeutic target.

records.title: WavPAC-Net: a wavelet-based hybrid encoder network with permuted axial-channel feature enhancement for liver segmentation
records.journal: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
records.abstract: The liver, core to human metabolism and detoxification, is threatened by chronic diseases like cirrhosis that increase hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk, with early diagnosis dependent on accurate liver segmentation in medical imaging. Current clinical segmentation methods generally suffer from low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and scarcity of AI-driven commercial products. Although deep learning technologies have been applied to liver segmentation, mainstream architectures still exhibit inherent limitations: CNN struggles with long-range dependencies while Transformer lacks fine detail representation. This study proposes WavPAC-Net, an innovative wavelet-based fusion network incorporating: (1) a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder combining ConvNeXt-Small branch for precise hepatic parenchymal texture capture and Swin Transformer branch for long-range dependency modeling; (2) a Wavelet Domain Fusion Module (WDFM) that decomposes the features extracted by CNN and Transformer into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands respectively, and performs adaptive weighted fusion; and (3) a Permuted Axial-Channel Feature Enhancer (PACFE) that implements cross-dimensional refinement of high-dimensional fused features through collaborative three-dimensional spatial modeling and channel dimension permutation. In systematic comparisons with 20 state-of-the-art segmentation models, WavPAC-Net demonstrates statistically significant advantages in both segmentation accuracy and boundary fidelity. Evaluated on the CirrMRI600+ dataset (T2-weighted MRI), WavPAC-Net achieved Dice score of 93.16%, IoU of 88.45%, and MCC of 93.03%, with a computational complexity of 19.88 GFLOPs. Multi-modal validation on the public LiTS CT dataset further confirmed the model’s excellent performance, achieving Dice score of 96.91%, IoU of 94.32%, and MCC of 96.79%. Overall, WavPAC-Net provides an effective balance between segmentation accuracy and computational complexity, supporting its potential for practical liver segmentation applications.

records.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI deep learning model combined with clinical model for noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
records.abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). Methods The internal development cohort comprised 334 surgically confirmed patients, including 231 patients with HCC and 103 with MF-ICC, and was divided at the patient level into a training cohort ( n = 233) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 101). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. Moreover, a clinical model was built based on independent predictors identified through multivariate analysis, which was ultimately integrated with the best-performing deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated and compared. Results Deep learning model directly feeding the three-phase images as a multi-channel input achieved better discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.814 in the internal validation cohort) than all single-phase and corresponding fusion models. The comprehensive 2D + multi-channel + clinical model showed the best performance for the differentiation of HCC from MF-ICC, achieving an AUC of 0.887 (95% CI, 0.819–0.954) in the internal validation cohort, and generalized well to the external validation cohort (AUC = 0.908; 95% CI, 0.811–1.000). However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.

records.title: Point-based liver and hepatic tumor segmentation and estimation
records.abstract:
Liver cancer is the fifth most common cancer in the world. Liver cancer is more serious in areas of western and central Africa and eastern and southeastern Asia. The average incidence of liver cancer in these areas is 20 per 100,000, and liver cancer is the third highest death cause from cancer. Roughly 20,000 new cases of liver cancer are diagnosed every year in the USA. If a very small lump tumor is found by early detection, treatment and curing may be easy, and human life can be prolonged. 
In this dissertation, point-based liver and hepatic tumor segmentation and estimation are presented in contrast enhanced (CE)-computed tomography (CT) images. Without having a reference image and training data, fully automatic segmentation of the liver structure and tumors using a reference point based on the spine is processed. Segmentation of the liver structure and tumors is performed regardless of pixel variation of CE-CT images involved by contrast agent. 
After obtaining CE-CT images, pre-processing such as histogram transformation and adaptive multi-modal threshold is performed. In order to process fully automatic segmentation for the liver structure and tumors, a reference point from the spine is defined. Liver segmentation using C-class maximum a posteriori decision and binary morphological filtering is processed. Partial histogram threshold algorithms are proposed in order to perform better liver segmentation. 
Finally, an inner small tumor is found, and large inner tumors using two statistical optimal thresholds are segmented. Boundary tumors of the liver are extracted by the bounding box and convex hull. Segmented tumors are evaluated by four basic possibilities, such as true negative, false positive, false negative, and true positive. As the evaluation measure, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy are calculated.

records.title: Liver And Hepatic Tumors Segmentation In 3-D Ct Images
records.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: Medical imaging is an important technique for diagnosis and treatment planning today. A new proposed method of fully automatic processing frameworks is given based on graph-cut and Geodesic Graph cut algorithms. This paper addresses the problem of segmenting liver and tumor regions from the abdominal CT images. A predicate is defined for measuring the evidence for a boundary between two regions using Geodesic Graph-based representation of the image. The algorithm is applied to image segmentation using two different kinds of local neighborhoods in constructing the graph. Liver and hepatic tumor segmentation can be automatically processed by the Geodesic graph-cut based method. This system has concentrated on finding a fast and interactive segmentation method for liver and tumor segmentation. In the preprocessing stage, the CT image process is carried over with mean shift filter and statistical thresholding method for reducing processing area with improving detections rate. Second stage is liver segmentation; the liver region has been segmented using the algorithm of the proposed method. The next stage tumor segmentation also followed the same steps. Finally the liver and tumor regions are separately segmented from the computer tomography image.

records.title: Hepatic Vein and Arterial Vessel Segmentation in Liver Tumor Patients
records.abstract: Preoperative observation of liver status in patients with liver tumors by abdominal Computed Tomography (CT) imaging is one of the essential references for formulating surgical plans. Preoperative vessel segmentation in the patient's liver region has become an increasingly important and challenging problem. Almost all existing methods first segment arterial and venous vessels on CT in the arterial and venous phases, respectively. Then, the two are directly registered to complete the reconstruction of the vascular system, ignoring the displacement and deformation of blood vessels caused by changes in body position and respiration in the two phases. We propose an unsupervised domain-adaptive two-stage vessel segmentation framework for simultaneous fine segmentation of arterial and venous vessels on venous phase CT. Specifically, we first achieve domain adaptation for arterial and venous phase CT using a modified cycle-consistent adversarial network. The newly added discriminator can improve the ability to generate and discriminate tiny blood vessels, making the domain-adaptive network more robust. The second-stage supervised training of arterial vessels was then performed on the translated arterial phase CT. In this process, we propose an orthogonal depth projection loss function to enhance the representation ability of the 3D U-shape segmentation network for the geometric information of the vessel model. The segmented venous vessels were also performed on venous phase CT in the second stage. Finally, we invited professional doctors to annotate arterial and venous vessels on the venous phase CT of the test set. The experimental results show that the segmentation accuracy of arterial and venous vessels on venous phase CT is 0.8454 and 0.8087, respectively. Our proposed framework can simultaneously achieve supervised segmentation of venous vessels and unsupervised segmentation of arterial vessels on venous phase CT. Our approach can be extended to other fields of medical segmentation, such as unsupervised domain adaptive segmentation of liver tumors at different CT phases, to facilitate the development of the community.

records.title: Deep segmentation of the liver and the hepatic tumors from abdomen tomography images
records.journal: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
records.abstract: A pipelined framework is proposed for accurate, automated, simultaneous segmentation of the liver as well as the hepatic tumors from computed tomography (CT) images. The introduced framework composed of three pipelined levels. First, two different transfers deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) are applied to get high-level compact features of CT images. Second, a pixel-wise classifier is used to obtain two output-classified maps for each CNN model. Finally, a fusion neural network (FNN) is used to integrate the two maps. Experimentations performed on the MICCAI’2017 database of the liver tumor segmentation (LITS) challenge, result in a dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 93.5% for the segmentation of the liver and of 74.40% for the segmentation of the lesion, using a 5-fold cross-validation scheme. Comparative results with the state-of-the-art techniques on the same data show the competing performance of the proposed framework for simultaneous liver and tumor segmentation.

records.title: Segmentations of Liver and Hepatic Tumors from 3D Computed Tomography Abdominal Images
records.abstract: The segmentation of liver using computed tomography (CT) data has gained a lot of importance in the medical image processing field. In this paper, we present a survey on liver segmentation methods and techniques using CT images for liver segmentation. An adaptive initialization method was developed to produce fully automatic processing frameworks based on graph-cut and gradient flow active contour algorithms. This method was applied to abdominal Computed Tomography (CT) images for segmentation of liver tissue and hepatic tumors. Twenty-five anonymized datasets were randomly collected from several radiology centres without specific request on acquisition parameter settings nor patient clinical situation as inclusion criteria. Resulting automatic segmentations of liver tissue and tumors were compared to their reference standard delineations manually performed by a specialist. Segmentation accuracy has been assessed through the following evaluation framework: dice similarity coefficient, false negative ratio, false positive ratio and processing time. The implemented initialization method allows fully automatic segmentation leading to superior overall performances of graph-cut algorithm in terms of accuracy and processing time. The initialization method here presented resulted suitable and reliable for two different segmentation techniques and could be further extended.

records.title: Fast segmentation and modeling of hepatic components for the planning of robot-assisted liver tumor ablation
records.journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
records.abstract: Segmentation and modeling of hepatic components from pre-operative images is very important for treatment planning and guidance in robot-assisted liver tumor ablation. An in-house developed system for hepatic component segmentation and modeling using CT data is presented in this paper. This system includes gross liver segmentation by a 3D mesh deformation model, liver vasculature segmentation by a vessel context-based voting and grouping method, liver tumor segmentation by a support vector machine framework, and other segmentation/modeling tool. This system was tested using 20 data sets from human patients and 5 sets of porcine CT scan. It is suggested by experimental results that the developed system is able to conduct fast segmentation and modeling of hepatic components for both human and large animal, with a satisfying accuracy, to support treatment planning.

records.title: A model integrating CEA and KRAS mutation statuses and computed tomography tumor-habitat radiomics predicts synchronous liver metastases in patients with rectal cancer: a dual-center study
records.abstract: Objective To investigate the diagnostic performance of a computed tomography (CT)-based habitat radiomics model for discriminating between patients with rectal cancer (RC) with and without synchronous liver metastases (SLM). Methods This retrospective study enrolled two independent patient cohorts. Cohort 1 (internal cohort) included 198 patients with pathologically confirmed RC with complete CT data from April 2022 to June 2025, comprising 46 SLM-positive and 152 SLM-negative cases. This cohort was divided randomly in a 7:3 ratio into a training set (140 patients: 33 SLM-positive, 107 SLM-negative) and an internal validation set (58 patients: 13 SLM-positive, 45 SLM-negative). Cohort 2 served as an external validation set, consisting of 55 patients with RC (18 SLM-positive, 37 SLM-negative). Regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated manually slice-by-slice on arterial-phase thin-slice CT images. Raw radiomics features were extracted from the ROIs and K-means clustering was implemented to segment tumor sub-habitats, followed by feature extraction for each sub-habitat. Feature-dimensionality reduction was performed on the training set using minimum redundancy maximum relevance and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator algorithms. Logistic regression classifiers were constructed to develop a conventional radiomics model and a habitat radiomics model, respectively. Model performance and clinical utility were quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified serum CEA and KRAS mutations as independent risk factors for SLM. These were integrated to build a clinical baseline model with AUC values of 0.730 (training set), 0.724 (internal validation set), and 0.701 (external validation set). After rigorous feature screening, 13 conventional radiomics features and 13 habitat radiomics features were retained for model construction. The conventional radiomics model yielded AUCs of 0.785 (training), 0.764 (internal validation), and 0.782 (external validation), while the habitat radiomics model achieved higher AUCs, with AUCs of 0.862, 0.826, and 0.826, respectively. The combined model integrating independent clinical risk factors and habitat radiomics score attained the numerically highest AUCs, with AUCs of 0.883 (training), 0.846 (internal validation), and 0.851 (external validation), outperforming the clinical, conventional radiomics, and standalone habitat models with robust cross-cohort stability. Calibration curves demonstrated favorable predictive consistency of the combined model, while DCA revealed sustained clinical net benefit across broad risk-threshold ranges. Conclusion A CT-based habitat radiomics model could effectively identify patients with RC with SLM, with performance numerically better than that of conventional whole-tumor radiomics. Integrating clinical biomarkers with habitat radiomics further increased the predictive accuracy, offering a novel non-invasive preoperative risk-stratification strategy for RC.

records.title: Nutritional value and total quality of sour curry powder, the most popular southern Thailand dish
records.abstract: As cross-cultural interactions continuously transform global dietary habits, the traditional Japanese rice seasoning (furikake) offers an innovative blueprint for Thai food product development. Inspired by this concept, a novel instant Thai sour curry rice topping was formulated. This product successfully integrates a high-protein nutritional profile with superior consumer palatability and extended storage stability. Key ingredients for Southern Thai sour curry paste including hot chili (Capsicum frutescens L.) shallot (Allium ascalonicum L.), garlic bulb (Allium sativum L.), lemongrass (Cymbopogon citratus (DC.) Stapf), and salt were blended, mixed with pre-cooked fish meat and souring agents tamarind pulp (Tamarindus indica L.) and dried cowa leaves (dried Garcinia cowa Roxb. ex Choisy leaves), stir-fried, and subsequently dried to yield the instant product. Results revealed that the combination of tamarind pulp and dried G. cowa Roxb leaves as a souring agent achieved the highest sensory acceptability (92%) and demonstrated high antioxidant activity. Nutritional analysis reveals that the final dehydrated product is rich in protein, yielding 39.45 ± 0.24%, while unsaturated fatty acids constitute a substantial portion (5.59 ± 0.05%) of the total lipid content (9.62 ± 0.08%). Furthermore, the sequential thermal treatment of stir-frying followed by hot air oven drying effectively minimized the microbial count, successfully complying with the safety standards established by the Thai FDA.

records.title: AI-assisted image-based screening identifies TFEB agonists that restore adipose angiogenesis and reduce adipose fibrosis
records.abstract: Adipose tissue expansion in obesity frequently outpaces vascularization, triggering hypoxia, fibrosis, and metabolic dysfunction. The molecular mechanisms coordinating adaptive angiogenesis during this expansion remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that myeloid deletion of Transcription Factor EB ( Tfeb ) in high-fat diet-fed mice exacerbates epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) dysfunction, manifesting as profound hypoxia, fibrosis, and systemic insulin resistance. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays reveal a novel TFEB-VEGFA axis: TFEB directly activates Vegfa transcription in macrophages, and its absence impairs angiogenic compensation under hypoxic stress. To translate these findings, we established an AI-driven, high-content screening platform to quantify TFEB nuclear translocation. We identified and validated Tetrandrine and Pacritinib as potent TFEB agonists. Notably, Tetrandrine acts via an mTOR-independent mechanism. Pharmacological activation of TFEB with these compounds restored adipose angiogenesis, resolved fibrosis, and improved insulin sensitivity in obese mice. These findings establish macrophage TFEB as a critical regulator of healthy adipose remodeling and validate the TFEB-VEGFA axis as a therapeutic target for metabolic diseases.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in pancreatic cancer surgery: evidence maturity, boundaries, and clinical translation
records.abstract: Pancreatic cancer surgery requires decisions about resectability, treatment sequencing, operative planning, complications, and prognosis. We mapped artificial intelligence (AI) studies to five surgical decision domains and evaluated study design, validation, performance, decision utility, workflow fit, and evidence limitations. This structured narrative review included 31 direct AI studies and three adjacent or protocol studies; only direct AI studies underwent evidence-maturity grading. Eighteen studies met Level 1, ten Level 2, and three Level 3; none reached Levels 4 or 5. Three-dimensional assessment of vascular involvement has undergone external and prospective performance validation, but its effect on surgical decisions or patient outcomes remains unproven. Automated segmentation can aid anatomical visualization, although tumor delineation and workflow demands limit use. Transcriptomic analyses of trial samples suggest differential adjuvant treatment benefit but do not establish prospective biomarker-guided treatment allocation. Models for complications, recurrence, and survival offer risk-stratification signals, yet calibration, actionable thresholds, class imbalance, and clinical utility remain concerns. AI should support radiologists, surgeons, and multidisciplinary teams rather than replace their judgment. Clinical adoption requires robust external validation, prospective workflow assessment, and evidence that AI-assisted decisions improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Global Landscape of Radiopharmaceutical Innovation: Emerging Targets and Molecules
records.abstract: ABSTRACT Following the recent commercial success of FDA‑approved targeted radiopharmaceuticals, an increasing number of pipeline candidates have advanced into clinical trials. Analyzing their development timelines, study durations, and clinical outcomes enables researchers to discern current trends and identify agents with promising commercial potential. This review provides a global overview of radiopharmaceutical development, with a focus on disease targets, radionuclides, ligand platforms, and clinical indications. Our analysis reveals that, alongside established targets such as PSMA and SSTR, emerging targets—including CAIX, GPC3, and DLL3—are broadening the spectrum of cancers amenable to radiopharmaceutical intervention. Concurrently, the adoption of therapeutic radionuclides with potent antitumor efficacy, particularly 225 Ac, 212 Pb, and 161 Tb, is gaining momentum. Examination of unsuccessful cases highlights persistent challenges, notably radionuclide supply constraints and in vivo toxicity. Encouragingly, regulatory frameworks are becoming more flexible to expedite development, and first‑in‑human studies offer an early opportunity to eliminate poor‑performing candidates before large‑scale trials. Nevertheless, there remains an urgent need for standardized clinical trial protocols to bridge the gap between clinical investigation and regulatory evaluation. Overall, this review aims to bridge the informational and technological gaps among laboratory–based basic research, hospital–based clinical trials, and industrial development, thereby offering insights for future progress and assisting in overcoming the obstacles facing radiopharmaceutical discovery.

records.title: Ameliorative Effect of Lycopene and Capsaicinoid Glucoside in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
records.journal: Journal of Biochemical and Molecular Toxicology
records.abstract: ABSTRACT Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a hematological malignancy with limited therapeutic efficacy, particularly in elderly and chemotherapy‐resistant patients. Although cytarabine and daunorubicin are the conventional treatments, their 5‐year survival rate is less than 15% in some populations. Nonetheless, natural bioactive substances with antileukemic properties might be a viable treatment strategy. The antileukemic potential of lycopene (Lyc) and capsaicinoid glucoside (CG), individually and in combination, is examined in this study as a possible adjuvant or alternative treatment. This study employed both in‐vitro (HL‐60 cell line) and in‐vivo (benzene‐induced leukemia rat model) methods. Cytotoxicity, apoptosis, and proliferation were evaluated in‐vitro using MTT assays, Trypan blue, crystal violet staining and flow cytometry (Annexin‐V/PI). Hematological parameters (WBC, RBC, neutrophils), oxidative stress indicators (SOD, GSH), qPCR and ELISA for anti‐apoptotic/proliferative markers (Bcl‐2, NF‐κB, Ki‐67, PCNA) were assessed in in vivo tests. To verify morphological alterations, blood smear analysis was carried out. Lyc and CG showed dose‐dependent cytotoxicity in vitro, synergistically Lyc+CG showed lowest cytotoxicity with IC 50 values of 21.35. Synergistic effects were shown by the Lyc+CG combination, which dramatically decreased cell viability and increased apoptosis (40.59% early apoptosis, 18.72% late apoptosis). In‐vitro and in‐vivo study showed that Lyc+CG reduced proliferation and anti‐apoptotic effect, restored SOD and GSH levels, and normalized haematological parameters ( p < 0.001). The Lyc+CG group's blood smears revealed more apoptotic bodies and fewer blast cells. By causing apoptosis, lowering oxidative stress, and preventing proliferation in cell line (HL‐60) and animal models (benzene‐induced leukemia in rats), the combination of Lyc and CG demonstrates strong antileukemic action. These results encourage more research into Lyc+CG as a possible AML treatment approach. To completely clarify its therapeutic potential, future research should concentrate on clinical trials and molecular insights.

records.title: Predicting complications after hepatectomy for hepatocellular carcinoma: a narrative review focused on liver failure
records.abstract: Hepatectomy is a potentially curative treatment for selected patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but postoperative complications remain an important source of morbidity and mortality. This narrative review focuses on prediction models for post-hepatectomy liver failure (PHLF), with additional discussion of selected non-PHLF complications. It emphasizes validation design, transportability, calibration, clinical actionability, and the distinction between evidence from HCC cohorts and cohorts with mixed diagnoses. PHLF has the most mature prediction literature because its risk is closely related to measurable liver reserve, portal hypertension, future liver remnant volume and function, and resection extent. Clinical and serum scores are accessible but generally provide moderate discrimination. Volumetric, functional, and imaging assessments add complementary information, whereas machine learning and radiomics models can capture nonlinear and high-dimensional patterns but often rely on small cohorts, random internal splits, and incomplete calibration reporting. Evidence for bile leakage includes validated clinical scores and a large externally validated machine learning model. Models for postoperative ascites, intra-abdominal infection or abscess, and surgical site infection remain sparse and are often perioperative rather than purely preoperative. Across endpoints, high apparent discrimination has not established clinical benefit. Future studies should prioritize standardized endpoints, adequate effective sample size, independent geographic external validation, calibration, net benefit assessment, and risk updating at successive stages. Current models should be used as decision support tools rather than substitutes for multidisciplinary clinical judgment.

records.title: CXCR2 associated neutrophil stromal interactions and immune exclusion in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer
records.abstract: Most microsatellite-stable or mismatch-repair-proficient colorectal cancers respond poorly to immune checkpoint monotherapy. This Mini Review examines whether C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (CXCR2)-associated neutrophil recruitment and local stromal interactions contribute to immune exclusion: CD8+ T cells accumulate in stroma or at the tumor margin with limited entry into epithelial nests. We propose that, in a subset of excluded lesions, recruited neutrophils acquire local functions that impair T-cell activity or access. Human observations and experimental perturbations support parts of this model; the complete pathway has not been established as a major cause of checkpoint resistance. Recruitment dependence, tissue adaptation, and measured function provide a basis for comparing studies with different neutrophil labels. Lesions selected for mechanistic investigation would need confirmed microsatellite-stable or mismatch-repair-proficient status, spatial exclusion, and a relevant intratumoral CXCR2-associated neutrophil program. Primary tumors and metastatic sites require separate evaluation. The limited activity of navarixin plus pembrolizumab argues against unselected targeting. Combining CXCR2 inhibition, selected stromal or vascular modulation, and checkpoint blockade remains a preclinical hypothesis. Before clinical translation, comparative studies must link intratumoral target engagement to improved CD8+ T-cell access, function, and tumor control. The proposed tissue biomarkers are research tools whose predictive value requires validation.

records.title: Spatial immune architecture and immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer
records.abstract: Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC), which accounts for most metastatic CRC, remains largely resistant to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Although low tumor mutational burden and limited neoantigen generation contribute to this resistance, the spatial organization of the tumor microenvironment may also influence antitumor immunity. This review examines mechanisms that establish immune-resistant architectures in MSS CRC, including insufficient T-cell priming, oncogenic signaling, suppressive myeloid niches, hypoxia, abnormal vasculature, and fibroblast-driven extracellular matrix remodeling. We discuss candidate spatial biomarkers, including compartment-specific T-cell distribution, T-cell–tumor-cell distances, multicellular immune neighborhoods, perivascular niches, and the organization and localization of tertiary lymphoid structures. We also examine how fibroblast heterogeneity, collagen architecture, hyaluronan accumulation, and vascular dysfunction can restrict T-cell access and function. Emerging studies associate selected spatial features with treatment outcomes, but the supporting evidence spans small treatment-specific cohorts, mixed CRC populations, and preclinical or non-CRC models. These findings therefore support spatial profiling as a complement to molecular and clinical biomarkers rather than an independently established basis for treatment selection. Prospective studies in defined treatment settings are needed to clarify the relationship between these spatial features and immunotherapy outcomes and to assess their potential to inform combination strategies in MSS CRC.
